title: Agent Runtime and CLI Architecture

milestones.name: CLI Command Model
milestones.objective: Refactor the existing Cobra CLI into explicit root, tui, run, server, and gnu command paths with stable flag semantics.
milestones.success: Root and tui open the TUI, run executes non-TUI, server and gnu are visible not-implemented commands, prompt no longer implies headless, and CLI parsing is centralized outside main.go.
milestones.diagram:
flowchart TD
    Root[squid-os root] --> TUI[tui command]
    Root --> Run[run command]
    Root --> Server[server command]
    Root --> GNU[gnu command]
    TUI --> Textarea[prefill textarea]
    Run --> NewRun[new run]
    Run --> Continue[continue session]
    Run --> AgentRun[named agent run]

tasks.name: Extract CLI command construction
tasks.what: Create an internal CLI package that builds the Cobra command tree and keeps main.go as a thin bootstrap.
tasks.why: Centralized command construction prevents CLI behavior from spreading through main.go as the command surface grows.
acceptance: main.go delegates command creation/execution to internal/cli.
Root, tui, run, server, and gnu commands are constructed in one package.
go build passes with no behavior changes beyond command routing.

tasks.name: Implement root and TUI option parsing
tasks.what: Add root and tui options for session selection, prompt prefill, model, thinking, working directory, agent system, tool, skill, and callable agent scopes.
tasks.why: TUI boot needs the same explicit session setup surface as run without treating prompt as headless execution.
acceptance: squid-os opens TUI.
squid-os tui opens TUI.
--prompt on root or tui pre-fills textarea and does not execute a run.
--session on root or tui opens the named saved session.
TUI bootstrap options are passed through a typed options object.

tasks.name: Implement complete run option parsing
tasks.what: Add run options for inline runs, named agents, session continuation, stdin composition, output mode, autosave, auth, memory, scopes, active skill, and limits.
tasks.why: run is the explicit non-TUI execution surface and must carry the full runtime override contract.
snippet:
type RunOptions struct {
    AgentName string
    PositionalAgent string
    SessionName string
    Prompt string
    Stdin string
    Mode string
    Model string
    Thinking string
    WorkingDir string
    AgentSystem string
    ToolNames []string
    SkillNames []string
    ActiveSkill string
    CallableAgentNames []string
    Autosave bool
    AutosaveName string
    AuthMode string
    MemoryNamespace string
    MemoryInstructions string
    Limits LimitOptions
}

type LimitOptions struct {
    MaxSteps int
    MaxTools int
    MaxTime string
    MaxToolResultTokens int
    MaxAgentDepth int
}
acceptance: squid-os run executes only through the explicit run command.
squid-os run name and squid-os run --agent name resolve equivalently.
Differing positional agent and --agent values fail clearly.
--prompt and stdin compose predictably.
--session adds a new turn to an existing session rather than rebuilding bootstrap.
Bootstrap replacement flags are rejected with --session where required by the prep docs.

tasks.name: Preserve version and stub commands
tasks.what: Wire --version to the canonical version source and expose server and gnu as help-visible not-implemented commands.
tasks.why: The expanded CLI must preserve existing version behavior while reserving future product surfaces cleanly.
acceptance: --version prints the canonical Squid-OS version and exits.
server appears in help and returns a clear not implemented response.
gnu appears in help as shell GNU tool generation migration surface and returns not implemented.

tasks.name: Add bash and zsh completion
tasks.what: Add shell completion for command names, static enum values, and dynamic sessions, skills, agents, and tool names where practical.
tasks.why: Completion is part of the CLI product contract and makes the larger command surface usable.
acceptance: --session completion suggests saved session names.
--skill and --skills completion suggest installed skills.
--agent and --agents completion suggest installed agents.
--tools completion suggests registered tools or a generated registry-backed list.
Static flags complete values for thinking, save, mode, memory namespace, and auth mode.

milestones.name: Agent Registry and Session Metadata
milestones.objective: Introduce global agents as first-class runtime presets with registry discovery, YAML loading, environment visibility, and session metadata.
milestones.success: Agents live under config agents, can be listed and loaded, appear in environment, and sessions persist root Agent plus available Agents separately from Skill and Skills.
milestones.diagram:
classDiagram
    class AgentDefinition
    class AgentRegistry
    class SessionAgent
    class SessionAgents
    AgentRegistry --> AgentDefinition
    SessionAgent --> AgentDefinition
    SessionAgents --> AgentRegistry

tasks.name: Add agent config path and registry
tasks.what: Create internal/agent with definition structs, YAML loading, registry scanning, and config path support for the agents directory.
tasks.why: Agents become a first-class global preset system like skills instead of a run-command special case.
acceptance: Paths includes an Agents directory under the Squid-OS config root.
EnsureDirs creates the agents directory.
Agents are stored as folders containing an agent.yaml file (same pattern as skills with SKILL.md).
Registry scans folders under agents dir and loads agent.yaml from each.
Registry lists agent names and descriptions.
Registry loads a full definition by name.
YAML uses gopkg.in/yaml.v3 (same as skills).

tasks.name: Add Agent and Agents session metadata
tasks.what: Extend SessionMeta with singular Agent provenance and plural Agents availability scope.
tasks.why: The root agent that started a session is provenance, while Agents is the callable subagent access list.
acceptance: Session Agent stores the root owning agent name without initial/current.
Session Agents stores initial/current callable agent names.
Agent remains distinct from Skill.
Agents remains distinct from Skills and Tools.

tasks.name: Expose agents in environment
tasks.what: Initialize the agent registry before session bootstrap and add an Agents section to the generated environment.
tasks.why: The model should discover available agents the same way it discovers skills.
acceptance: Environment includes an Agents section with name and description.
Agent registry initialization happens before NewSession environment injection.
Existing Skills environment behavior remains unchanged.

milestones.name: Runtime Options and Turn Preparation
milestones.objective: Resolve settings, agent definitions, CLI options, and session continuation into concrete session/run options, then prepare each turn consistently before streaming.
milestones.success: TUI, run, session continuation, and agent tools use the same resolved options and transition injection happens after the user message and before stream start.
milestones.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Entry as CLI or TUI
    participant Resolve as ResolveOptions
    participant Session as ChatSession
    participant Turn as PrepareTurn
    participant Loop as RunLoop
    Entry->>Resolve: settings agent flags session
    Resolve->>Session: create or load session
    Entry->>Session: append user message
    Entry->>Turn: desired next turn options
    Turn->>Session: inject transitions
    Entry->>Loop: stream prepared session

tasks.name: Add runtime option resolver
tasks.what: Add a small resolver that maps settings, optional agent definition, CLI options, and session continuation context into concrete runtime options.
tasks.why: One resolver prevents precedence, model parsing, autosave, auth, and scope rules from diverging across TUI, run, and agent tools.

Agent definition values override settings defaults.
Combined provider/model strings are parsed consistently.

Resolved options include tools, skills, active skill, callable agents, autosave, auth, memory, limits, and agent depth.
Root runs default AgentDepth to Limits.MaxAgentDepth (default 5).
Agent depth is decremented for each nested call_agent invocation.

tasks.why: Session creation should receive explicit inputs for agent, scopes, memory, autosave, auth, and limits instead of reading scattered global state.

New sessions can set active Skill separately from available Skills.

tasks.name: Add shared PrepareTurn
tasks.what: Move next-turn transition injection into a shared PrepareTurn function called after user append and before StartStream.
tasks.why: Model, thinking, active skill, and availability changes must behave the same in TUI, run, session continuation, and future automation.
acceptance: PrepareTurn inserts transitions immediately after the user message they affect.
TUI sendMessage no longer owns model/thinking/skill transition logic.
run --session uses PrepareTurn before streaming.
StartStream remains focused on starting provider streaming and does not hide history mutation.

tasks.name: Model autosave as session runtime config
tasks.what: Represent autosave settings in resolved options and session metadata so TUI and run can persist automatically through one concept.
tasks.why: Autosave is the existing persistence behavior and should replace incognito-style special cases and run-only save wording.
acceptance: Resolved runtime options include autosave enabled and optional autosave name.
Session metadata can persist autosave configuration.
Manual save remains separate from autosave.
Existing TUI autosave behavior can be mapped to the new config.

milestones.name: Memory Foundation
milestones.objective: Add memory namespace config, path resolution, session metadata, and environment exposure without implementing a full memory engine.
milestones.success: workspace, global, and agent memory resolve to clear paths, memory instructions appear in environment, and memory metadata persists on sessions.
milestones.diagram:
flowchart TD
    Agent[agent memory config] --> Resolve[resolve memory]
    CLI[CLI memory override] --> Resolve
    Settings[settings memory dir] --> Resolve
    WorkDir[working directory] --> Resolve
    Resolve --> Session[session memory metadata]
    Resolve --> Env[environment memory section]

tasks.name: Add memory config and namespace paths
tasks.what: Create internal/memory with config types and helpers that resolve workspace, global, and agent namespaces to concrete paths.
tasks.why: Memory needs a stable structural foundation before any retrieval or writeback engine exists.
acceptance: workspace namespace resolves to working-directory/memory.
global namespace resolves to configured memory dir.
agent namespace resolves under config agents agent-name memory.
No memory retrieval or writeback engine is added in this task.

tasks.name: Persist and expose memory config
tasks.what: Add memory metadata to sessions and update environment generation to show namespace, resolved path, instructions, and current memory index content.
tasks.why: The model needs explicit memory intent and location even while the memory engine remains deferred.
acceptance: Session metadata stores resolved memory namespace, path, and instructions.
Environment includes memory namespace and resolved path.
Environment includes memory instructions when configured.
Existing memory index display still works.

milestones.name: Run Execution and Output Modes
milestones.objective: Make run execute prepared sessions through the shared loop with autosave, session continuation, auth mapping, limits, and output modes.
milestones.success: run supports final_message, silent, stream JSONL, structured not implemented, autosaves saved runs, and keeps stdout/stderr contracts clean.
milestones.diagram:
flowchart TD
    Run[run command] --> Resolve[resolve options]
    Resolve --> Session[create or load session]
    Session --> Turn[prepare turn]
    Turn --> Loop[run loop]
    Loop --> Output[output adapter]
    Loop --> Autosave[autosave if enabled]

tasks.name: Build run execution service
tasks.what: Create a run package that creates or loads a session, appends prompt input, prepares the turn, runs RunLoop, and applies autosave. Replaces and deprecates internal/headless.
tasks.why: run should become the canonical non-TUI execution path. There should be one way to run things — internal/headless is deprecated and its functionality is absorbed here.
acceptance: run executes a fresh inline prompt without launching TUI.
run with a named agent creates a session from that agent.
run --session appends a new turn to an existing saved session.
autosave writes a session when enabled and reports only the saved session name.

tasks.name: Implement run output modes
tasks.what: Add output adapters for final_message, silent, stream, and structured mode handling.
tasks.why: Automation needs predictable stdout and stderr behavior for each run mode.
acceptance: final_message prints the final assistant answer to stdout.
silent prints no final assistant answer to stdout.
saved session name goes to stderr for final_message and silent when autosaved.
structured returns a clear not implemented error for phase 1.

tasks.name: Add CLI stream JSONL protocol
tasks.what: Map loop events and selected session lifecycle events into JSONL stream output with timestamps, roles, message IDs, and tool call IDs.
tasks.why: stream mode needs a stable machine-readable CLI boundary without redesigning provider streaming.
acceptance: stream emits session_start as the first JSONL event.
session_start includes saved session name only when saved.
stream events include timestamps.
message, thinking, tool call, tool execution, permission request, error, session_event, and finished events are valid JSONL.
stream mode does not duplicate saved session metadata to stderr on success.

tasks.name: Apply run auth and limits
tasks.what: Map agent/run auth modes onto existing authorization behavior and enforce practical phase-1 run limits.
tasks.why: Non-TUI runs and agent tools must be deterministic and bounded without inventing separate auth or limit systems.
acceptance: max tool result tokens continues to be enforced.
max steps, max tools, and max time are modeled and enforced where practical.
max_agent_depth is enforced — defaults to 5, decrements with each call_agent, returns error at 0.
auth-required behavior maps to configured non-TUI policy.
No separate agent-tool auth subsystem is introduced.

milestones.name: Agent Tools
pattern: Tool Adapter, Registry Guard, Blocking Delegation
milestones.objective: Add list_agents, call_agent, and inline_agent tools using the agent registry and run execution model.
milestones.success: The model can list agents, call an allowed named agent as a blocking final-answer subtask, and run inline agent definitions from tool arguments.
milestones.diagram:
flowchart TD
    Parent[parent session] --> Tool[agent tool]
    Tool --> List[list_agents]
    Tool --> Call[call_agent]
    Tool --> Inline[inline_agent]
    Call --> RunNamed[run named agent]
    Inline --> RunInline[run inline profile]
    RunNamed --> Result[final answer result]
    RunInline --> Result

tasks.name: Register list_agents tool
tasks.what: Add a list_agents tool that returns agent names and descriptions using the agent registry and documented callable-agent behavior.
tasks.why: The model needs explicit agent discovery just like it has skill_list for skills.
acceptance: list_agents is registered in the tool registry.
list_agents returns the callable subset — agents allowed by current session Agents scope.
Mirrors skill_list behavior: shows what is actually usable in current context.

tasks.name: Register call_agent tool
tasks.what: Add call_agent as a blocking named-agent tool with arguments for agent name, prompt, and limits.
tasks.why: Provides simple phase-1 sub-agent delegation while keeping full child-session orchestration out of scope.
acceptance: call_agent requires agent and prompt.
call_agent accepts limits for the delegated subtask.
call_agent rejects agents not allowed by the current session Agents scope.
call_agent checks agent depth from parent context; returns error when depth is 0.
call_agent decrements depth by 1 and passes remaining depth to the child.
called agent uses its own configured tools, skills, agents, memory, system, and model.
call_agent returns only the final answer as the tool result.

tasks.name: Register inline_agent tool
tasks.what: Add inline_agent as a blocking tool whose agent-like profile is defined directly in tool arguments instead of an installed preset.
tasks.why: Supports ad hoc delegation without requiring users to create a registry agent file first.
acceptance: inline_agent does not require registry lookup.
inline_agent profile source is the tool arguments.
inline_agent runs blocking and returns the final answer.
inline_agent uses the normal run execution path.

milestones.name: Cleanup and Validation
milestones.objective: Remove obsolete incognito and legacy CLI behavior, then validate the new architecture with focused regression tests.
milestones.success: Incognito and implicit headless prompt behavior are gone, version remains preserved, and tests cover CLI parsing, agents, runtime resolution, PrepareTurn, run output, and agent tools.
milestones.diagram:
flowchart TD
    Legacy[legacy CLI behavior] --> Remove[remove hidden mode switches]
    Incognito[incognito mode] --> Autosave[explicit autosave config]
    Tests[focused tests] --> Build[go build and go test]
    Build --> Done[ready for implementation review]

tasks.name: Drop incognito CLI flag
tasks.what: Remove the incognito CLI flag from main.go. Incognito toggle (alt+i) remains in the app — it keeps the session alive and just stops saving/history.
tasks.why: The incognito feature is useful for privacy (no history, no save). Keep it as an in-app toggle, just remove the CLI startup flag.
acceptance: No incognito flag in CLI argument parsing.
App still toggles incognito via alt+i.
Incognito still blocks history and session saves.
Toggle off reloads session from disk (discarding incognito changes).

tasks.name: Remove legacy root CLI behavior
tasks.what: Remove implicit headless-on-prompt behavior and legacy root image handling that no longer fit the explicit command model. internal/headless is deprecated — its functionality is absorbed by internal/run and the new CLI command tree.
tasks.why: Root command should consistently mean TUI while non-TUI execution belongs only under run. There should be one way to run things.
acceptance: Root --prompt does not start non-TUI execution.
Non-TUI execution requires the run command.
Unsupported legacy flags are removed or rejected clearly.

tasks.name: Add focused regression tests
tasks.what: Add tests for CLI parsing, agent registry loading, runtime precedence, PrepareTurn injection, run outputs, memory paths, and agent tools.
tasks.why: The new architecture crosses many entrypoints and needs tests to prevent behavior drift.
acceptance: Tests cover positional agent and --agent equivalence and conflict.
Tests cover --prompt plus stdin composition.
Tests cover --session continuation rejecting bootstrap replacement flags.
Tests cover PrepareTurn transition placement.
Tests cover stream session_start output and saved session name behavior.
Tests cover agent registry scan/load and agent tool contracts.

problem: Squid-OS needs a clean explicit CLI, first-class agent presets, session continuation, autosave-aware run execution, memory scaffolding, and bounded agent tool delegation without scattering behavior across main.go and TUI-only paths.
goal: A mode-driven CLI, global agent registry, expanded session metadata, shared turn preparation, memory namespace foundation, run output modes, autosave behavior, and phase-1 agent tools.
